To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gravitational coupling constant decreases with time, and the cosmological constant decreases with time.
we have obtained exact solutions for the Bianchi type- I and III, V, Kantowski-Sachs, and VIo models in scalar-tensor theories of gravity with a time-dependent cosmologial constant.

“In a family of scalar tensor theories, the gravitational constant decreases with the time and the cosmological constant also decreases with time so these models are compatible with the Dirac hypothesis.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a class of gravitational theories which contain the Einstein theory of gravity and a scalar field as particular cases.
the study of a family of scalar tensor theories of gravity with a time-dependent “cosmological” constant.
a family of scalar–tensor theories with a dynamic cosmological constant and the corresponding cosmological models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scalar-tensor theory with a time-dependent cosmologic constant is a very good theory of the Universe.
the scalar-tensor theory with a cosmological term is an interesting alternative to general relativity.
, in the context of the theory of gravity, the cosmological constant is not an independent parameter but is related to the gravitational constant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scalar-tensor theories with time-dependent cosmological constants can provide an alternative to the inflationary scenario.
a time-dependent cosmolog-ical constant can be used to unify the gravitational constant and the cosmological constant.
the scalar-tensor theories with the dynamic cosmological constant are compatible with the Dirac hypothesis and with the observational data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time-dependent cosmological term can have a very important effect in the dynamics of cosmological models.
a time dependent cosmological constant can be accommodated in a class of scalar-tensor models.
the scalar-tensor theories can explain the late-time acceleration without the introduction of a time-varying cosmological constant.
